name: CRESST cryogenic calorimeter array
notes: No page consulted gives the number of modules in operation or a precise operating temperature (mK).

placements.locator: official site, 'A Short History of CRESST'
placements.quote: led to the proposal of a dark matter search experiment using cryogenic calorimeters with transition edge sensors in the LNGS underground laboratory in 1993.

isotope.value: CaWO4 (CRESST-II/III main target); sapphire (Al2O3) in CRESST-I; lithium aluminate modules also deployed in CRESST-III

temperature.note: Stated as around 15 mK in the introduction of the cited paper (approximate, hence approx=true).
temperature.quote: CRESST utilises cryogenic calorimeters operated at around 15 mK.

threshold.note: CRESST-III threshold; the source states 'and lower' rather than a single hard number.
threshold.quote: The advancement in W-TES sensors allowed the CRESST detectors to reach energy thresholds of 10 eV and lower, opening the way to the exploration of dark matter masses as low as 70 MeV/c2.

summary.plain: Small crystals, some no heavier than a coin, cooled colder than outer space and watched for the tiny flash of light and warmth made when a particle bumps an atom inside.
summary.technical: Cryogenic transition-edge-sensor calorimeters on scintillating crystal absorbers: sapphire in CRESST-I (2000-2003), 300 g CaWO4 crystals in CRESST-II (2003-2019), and ~25 g CaWO4/Al2O3/LiAlO4 crystals in CRESST-III (from 2019) reaching nuclear-recoil thresholds of 10 eV and lower.

technology.quote: the simultaneous read-out of the deposited energy in the main absorber and an associated light signal
technology.value: Cryogenic calorimeters with tungsten transition-edge sensors (TES) on scintillating crystal absorbers (sapphire in CRESST-I; CaWO4 from CRESST-II on), reading both a phonon (heat) and a scintillation-light channel
